events.title: Edict of Nantes Issued
events.description: King Henry IV of France issued the Edict of Nantes. It granted the Protestant Huguenots substantial rights to practice their faith after decades of religious war.
events.significance: It was one of Europe's earliest major steps toward religious tolerance. It set an important precedent for coexistence within a single state.

events.title: Thomas Jefferson Is Born
events.description: Thomas Jefferson was born in colonial Virginia. He grew up to draft the Declaration of Independence and serve as the third President of the United States.
events.significance: Jefferson's writings shaped American ideals of liberty and self-government. His presidency doubled the nation's size through the Louisiana Purchase.

events.title: Fort Sumter Surrenders
events.description: After a bombardment that began on April 12, Union forces at Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor surrendered to Confederate troops.
events.significance: The surrender ended the first battle of the American Civil War. It galvanized both North and South as the conflict began in earnest.

events.title: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre
events.description: In Amritsar, India, British troops under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer opened fire on a large crowd of unarmed civilians. Hundreds were killed.
events.significance: The massacre hardened Indian opinion against British rule. It became a turning point in the Indian independence movement.

events.title: Apollo 13 Suffers an Explosion
events.description: An oxygen tank exploded aboard Apollo 13 while it was on its way to the Moon. The spacecraft was crippled, and the crew had to abandon their lunar landing.
events.significance: The crew's safe return to Earth, after improvised repairs and round-the-clock work by mission control, is remembered as one of NASA's finest hours.
